data.Basic Foraging: Ability to identify and collect edible berries in a natural environment.
data.Water Source Location: Skill in finding and utilizing natural water sources such as streams to maintain hydration.

data.Herb Foraging: Ability to identify and gather edible wild herbs in a natural environment.

data.Resource Management: Skill in assessing and prioritizing resource needs (hunger and thirst) effectively based on current environment and health status.
data.Wildlife Awareness: Enhanced ability to recognize changing wildlife behavior and adjust actions to minimize risk.
data.Sustainable Resource Collection: Skill in collecting resources in a way that considers future availability and environmental impact.

data.Advanced Resource Management: Improved ability to manage resources like water and food even when availability is limited, taking into account personal health conditions such as minor injuries and illness.
data.Strategic Foraging: Enhanced skill in prioritizing and gathering the most accessible food sources based on the environment's current conditions and potential changes, respecting wildlife behavior.
data.Environmental Adaptation: Skill in adjusting actions and strategies to effectively sustain health and energy levels by understanding the environmental shifts and planning for future necessities such as shelter.

data.Shelter Construction: Ability to create and establish a suitable shelter using natural resources such as thick forest coverage and rock formations, considering environmental conditions and personal health needs.
